decision_reason: The closest unseen pair, Elevator Up and Elevator Down, differs only in smoothness and impulsiveness. Travel direction would be a meaningful additional distinction, but the supplied hip IMU capabilities do not establish reliable signed vertical velocity: constant-speed travel provides little inertial evidence, and acceleration direction depends on the travel phase. Walking Left and Walking Right also have closely related A1 descriptions, but a transferable signed lateral distinction would require assumptions about body-relative alignment and whether the labels denote side-stepping or turning. Elevator Down has the weakest seen coverage, yet adding direction semantics would not establish observable transfer from stair locomotion to passive transport. After comparing the supplied prototypes, no additional independent ordinal attribute has sufficiently clear discriminability and predictability to justify changing A1. Preserve the existing ontology without treating its class-level asymmetries as measured sensor differences.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall hip acceleration and rotation magnitude. Retains the broad walking-versus-passive-transport contrast and transfer from walking and stationary seen anchors. Ambiguity arises because smooth transport can have little inertial excitation despite substantial displacement, and incidental body movement can increase intensity.

cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in hip motion, allowing transfer of gait periodicity from Walking Right and stair activities to unseen walking. It distinguishes repeated locomotor cycles from elevator travel without inventing a direction cue. Ambiguity includes short windows, weak cycles, and multiple observable oscillations per movement unit.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes in hip inertial signals, preserving a concept distinct from isolated impacts. Standing and Walking Downstairs provide transferable smooth-versus-fluctuating anchors. The supplied Elevator Up versus Elevator Down distinction remains a semantic hypothesis: travel direction alone does not imply different smoothness, and transport phase or incidental movement can dominate.

impulsiveness: G10 supports brief abrupt changes at the hip, retaining transfer from impact-rich Walking Downstairs and Jumping Up versus quiet Standing. It complements sustained smoothness rather than replacing it. Elevator transients may be absent from a window, and direction alone does not establish stronger peaks for Elevator Down; the supplied pair distinction is not guaranteed observable.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative hip orientation as partial evidence for global posture. Retains upright seen anchors for unseen walking and elevator activities and a broad contrast with Sleeping. A single hip sensor cannot fully determine load-bearing configuration; seated trunk posture, pelvic tilt, and mounting orientation make fine ordinal distinctions uncertain.

posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative hip orientation. Preserves transfer between nearly fixed upright posture and changing locomotor configurations without adding unsupported directional labels. Local pelvic movement is not equivalent to global postural change, so Walking Left versus Walking Forward differences and transfer from Walking Right remain uncertain.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular motion at the hip, retaining a potentially transferable contrast between locomotor rotation and quiet standing or elevator transport. Walking Right is a relevant seen anchor for Walking Left. Side labels alone do not establish turning or greater rotation, and pelvic oscillation can occur without a heading change; therefore no signed rotation refinement is justified.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translational-motion evidence, preserving the semantic distinction between transport and stationary posture and transfer from seen locomotion. Predictability is limited: steady elevator velocity is not directly observable from acceleration, and short-window proxies do not establish sustained displacement or its sign. Retain the existing concept rather than introduce an unreliable up-versus-down refinement.

motion_regularity: G11 supports recurrence and temporal predictability independently of repetition rate. Retains transfer from consistent walking or quiet standing to unseen walking and transport. Short windows and near-static signals can make regularity ambiguous, while class labels alone do not guarantee different regularity for Walking Left and Walking Forward.

semantic_redundancy_review: The nine retained concepts are related but not identical: intensity measures magnitude, cadence measures repetition rate, regularity measures predictability, smoothness measures sustained fluctuations, and impulsiveness measures brief peaks. Mean posture differs from posture variation, and rotation differs from translation. A gait-periodicity addition would substantially overlap cadence and regularity. Signed lateral or vertical travel could be semantically discriminative but lacks sufficiently established, stable observability here. The elevator pair therefore remains potentially confusable; no artificial separation or improvement in coverage is claimed.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
